newsitem.title: USA: US spot Gulf jet fuel rallies anew on refiner buys.
newsitem.headline: US spot Gulf jet fuel rallies anew on refiner buys.

text.p: Gulf Coast jet fuel differentials continued their week-long rally Wednesday, firming almost 1.5 cents a gallon as several majors searched for tight barrels, players said.

"There's no question they're stronger. It looks like a few people are caught short," one Gulf player said, noting today is the scheduling deadline for nominating front-third-cycle material for delivery on the Colonial Pipeline.
Traders said Exxon, Koch Oil, Citgo and Conoco had all been seeking third-cycle 54-grade barrels, adding that some buyers seemed already well supplied with low-sulfur 55 grade jet fuel.

"There's some nervousness over low supplies, which may account for some of the buying" of 54-grade, a Gulf trader said, who pegged offers as high as 2.00 cents over the February print by midday Wednesday.
Market players said the strength in 54-grade appeared to be localized on the prompt barrels, with little buying interest noted for later February supplies.

Some players cited unconfirmed rumors of refinery output problems, while others ascribed growing differential strength to crimped supplies brought on by ongoing refinery maintenance turnarounds in the Gulf.
"It's very difficult to gauge because it's such a small market. Volatility is always very high," said one trader.
Gulf Coast 54-grade diffs have firmed almost three cents since last Thursday, boosted by refiner buying.
Gulf 55-grade diffs firmed one cent Wednesday to between 2.0 and 2.25 cents over the print for front-third cycle material, buoyed by the stronger diffs on 54-grade, traders said.
New York Harbor 54-grade was traded Wednesday for 4.50 cents over February futures, stable with Tuesday levels, but 1.50 cents firmer than a week ago.
